title: Compare an initial henselian local algebra with an ind-etale local model and transfer presentations
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a commutative local ring, where $k=R/\mathfrak m$. Let $C,H$ be henselian local rings [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] with local structural maps $\eta_C:R\to C$ and $\eta_H:R\to H$; a map of local rings is local when the inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal. Suppose that $R\to C$ is ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] and that its structural residue map $e_C:k\to k_C=C/\mathfrak m_C$ is an isomorphism. Assume only the following universal property for $H$: for every henselian local ring $T$ and local map $a:R\to T$, there is exactly one local map $b:H\to T$ with $b\eta_H=a$. Then there are unique local $R$-algebra maps $f:C\to H$ and $g:H\to C$, with $gf=\mathrm{id}_C$ and $fg=\mathrm{id}_H$. In particular $f$ is an isomorphism over the specified maps from $R$; no residue-field identification or etale-colimit presentation of $H$ is assumed. Moreover, for any commutative ring $P$ with a ring map $P\to R$, any small filtered diagram $(D_i)$ of commutative $P$-algebras, and any colimit cocone $(C,(\lambda_i:D_i\to C))$ of its underlying rings inducing the specified composite $P\to R\to C$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], the maps $f\lambda_i:D_i\to H$ make $H$ a colimit of the same diagram both in rings and in commutative $P$-algebras, for the composite $P\to R\to H$. If all $D_i$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and finitely presented over $P$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], this gives an ind-etale presentation of that specified map $P\to H$.

proof.text: Let $a:R\to T$ be any local map with $T$ henselian local, and write $k_T=T/\mathfrak m_T$, $e_T:k\to k_T$ for its residue map. Set $\tau=e_Te_C^{-1}:k_C\to k_T$. Locality gives $\eta_C^{-1}(\mathfrak m_C)=a^{-1}(\mathfrak m_T)=\mathfrak m$, and $\tau e_C=e_T$. By [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], $C$ is a filtered colimit of etale $R$-algebras. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] with $S=T$, $A=C$, $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_C$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$, identifying residue fields at maximal ideals with local-ring quotients. It gives a unique local $R$-map $C\to T$ inducing $\tau$. Every local $R$-map $h:C\to T$ induces $\bar h$ with $\bar h e_C=e_T$, hence $\bar h=\tau$. Thus uniqueness holds among all local $R$-maps, with no residue condition imposed separately.

source.place: Tag 08HR (lemma-map-into-henselian-colimit), applied at maximal ideals; agent specialization to a local algebra with unchanged residue field.

proof.text: Take $T=H$ and $a=\eta_H$ in Step 1 to obtain the unique local $R$-map $f:C\to H$. The assumed initial property of $H$ gives the unique local $R$-map $g:H\to C$. Composites are local since inverse images of maximal ideals compose. Both $gf$ and $\mathrm{id}_C$ are local $R$-maps $C\to C$, so Step 1 with $T=C$ gives $gf=\mathrm{id}_C$. Both $fg$ and $\mathrm{id}_H$ extend $\eta_H$ as local maps $H\to H$, so the initial property of $H$ gives $fg=\mathrm{id}_H$. These identities and $f\eta_C=\eta_H$, $g\eta_H=\eta_C$ give the required unique inverse isomorphisms over $R$.

source.place: Tag 08HR (lemma-map-into-henselian-colimit), applied at maximal ideals; agent specialization to a local algebra with unchanged residue field.

proof.text: For the specified diagram, put $\mu_i=f\lambda_i$. For a transition $d_{ij}$, $\mu_jd_{ij}=f\lambda_jd_{ij}=f\lambda_i=\mu_i$, so this is a ring cocone. Given any compatible ring maps $t_i:D_i\to B$, [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives a unique ring map $u:C\to B$ with $u\lambda_i=t_i$. Set $v=ug:H\to B$; then $v\mu_i=ugf\lambda_i=t_i$. If $w:H\to B$ also satisfies these equations, $(wf)\lambda_i=t_i$ for all $i$, hence $wf=u$ by the same universal property, and $w=wfg=ug=v$. This proves the full ring-colimit assertion.

source.place: Tag 002F (definition-colimit), explicit verification of the cocone universal property.

proof.text: Write $s_i:P\to D_i$, $\rho_C:P\to C$, $\rho_H:P\to H$ for the specified structures. By hypothesis $\lambda_is_i=\rho_C$, and $R$-linearity gives $f\rho_C=\rho_H$, $g\rho_H=\rho_C$. Hence $\mu_is_i=\rho_H$. If the $t_i$ of Step 3 are $P$-algebra maps to $(B,\rho_B)$, choose one index $i$; filteredness includes nonemptiness by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then $u\rho_C=u\lambda_is_i=t_is_i=\rho_B$, so $v\rho_H=ug\rho_H=u\rho_C=\rho_B$. Thus the unique ring mediator is a $P$-algebra map. Its ring uniqueness implies $P$-algebra uniqueness, proving the second colimit assertion.

source.place: Tag 002F (definition-colimit), explicit verification of the cocone universal property.

proof.text: If every $D_i$ is etale and finitely presented over $P$, the small filtered colimit presentation of Step 4 is exactly an ind-etale presentation by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Its structural map is $\rho_H=P\to R\xrightarrow{\eta_H}H$ by the cocone equations above, so it proves the final assertion for the specified map.
